title: The Manson Family Murders Part I
summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about Charles Manson and the Manson family, then cover the 1969 Tate and La Bianca murders in Los Angeles: the Cielo Drive house attack, the Labianca killings, and the Helter Skelter race-war motive. They trace the earlier Gary Hinman murder and the July 1 Crow shooting, then Manson's troubled childhood, institutionalization, rise in San Francisco and Los Angeles, his ties to Dennis Wilson and the music industry, and the family's life at Spahn Ranch. The episode ends on a cliffhanger, with part two to cover the Beatles' White Album.

segments.title: Opening banter and Manson's music ambitions
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck joke about the family's wholesome image and set up the episode. They discuss the urban legend that Manson was rejected from the Monkees, which is false, and the theory that his frustrated music career motivated the murders. They also reflect on Manson's cultural image as a kid in the 1980s and how the murders were seen as the end of the hippie era.

segments.title: Tate murders at Cielo Drive
segments.summary: On the night of August 8-9, 1969, Tex Watson, Susan Atkins and Patricia Krenwinkel entered the Cielo Drive house. Linda Kasabian waited outside as driver. Steven Parent was shot before entering. Inside, Sharon Tate, Abigail Folger, Voytek Frykowski and Jay Sebring were killed. The hosts describe the brutal scene, the words written in blood, and Manson's directive to destroy everyone there.

segments.title: LaBianca murders
segments.summary: Two nights later, Manson sent the family to kill again. They went to the LaBianca house in Los Angeles, where Leno and Rosemary LaBianca were killed. Manson took part in tying them up and then left. The family wrote words in blood, including Death to Pigs and Helter Skelter, and the Rise notion was discussed as a plan to start a race war.

segments.title: Gary Hinman murder and Bernard Crowe shooting
segments.summary: Before the Tate and LaBianca murders, the family killed Gary Hinman in late July 1969. Bobby Beausoleil was arrested driving Hinman's car, and Manson was present for the killing, which involved cutting off part of Hinman's ear. Earlier, on July 1, Manson shot Bernard Crowe, a drug dealer he believed was a Black Panther, but Crowe survived and did not go to police. The hosts link this to the political piggies writing at the Hinman scene and to the race war theory.

segments.title: Recap and Charles Manson's childhood and prison years
segments.summary: The hosts recap the murders. They describe Manson's childhood, born in 1934 to a teenage mother, with a father who was absent and an alcoholic mother who was in and out of jail. He was institutionalized from an early age, and was released from federal prison in 1967. They discuss his probable schizophrenia and paranoid delusional disorder.

segments.title: Manson in San Francisco and the family's formation
segments.summary: After his release, Manson went to San Francisco, where he attracted followers during the hippie era. His first partner was Mary Brunner, and he later gathered women and men, including Lynette Squeaky Fromme, into a group. The family lived by stealing, prostitution and dumpster food, and Manson held mesmerizing nighttime talks around bonfires.

segments.title: Dennis Wilson, Terry Melcher and Spahn Ranch
segments.summary: Manson moved the family to Los Angeles to pursue a recording career. Dennis Wilson of the Beach Boys picked up female followers and let the family stay at his house for a few months. Through Wilson, Manson met record producers including Terry Melcher, who had once lived at the Tate house. The family then moved to Spahn Ranch, an old western film set, and used Barker Ranch in Death Valley. The episode ends on a cliffhanger about the Beatles' White Album, to be covered in part two.

segments.title: Outro
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck tease part two on the Beatles' White Album and invite listener feedback.
